newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up, boosted by Lek, Dolenjska. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up, boosted by Lek, Dolenjska. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]

text.p: Slovenian shares ended the week 0.76 percent higher on Friday, driven mainly by strong demand for drug maker Lek and a nearly 10 percent jump in bank Dolenjska.
But traders said volume remained slack as fresh money continued to stay away.
The SBI index rose 10.13 points (corrects from 10.13 percent) or 0.76 percent to 1,350.78. In the course of the week the index rose by 1.32 percent.
"Prices are most likely to stay at current levels until fresh information about foreign investment is available, which could happen in the beginning of May," one broker said.

In February the central bank blocked foreign investment by ordering foreign portfolio investors to open special custodian account at one of Slovenia's 14 fully licensed banks in order to be able to trade in Slovenian securities.
Since then the index has about 19 percent, while average daily share trading volume fell to 70 million from 500 million.
Overall 11 shares rose, four fell and three were flat, while nine were untraded. Turnover eased to 56.4 million tolars from 57.6 million.
Drug maker Lek's A issue was the most actively traded, gaining 1.08 percent to 25,380 tolars on volume of 2,476 shares.

Traders said Lek remained one of the most interesting shares on the market, because of its good performance and that it would probably attract a big share of eagerly expected fresh foreign investment.

Dolenjska Bank's preferred shares were the top gainer, jumping 9.92 percent to 13,850 tolars on volume of 480 shares. Traders attributed the jump to the bank's good business results reported on Thursday.
Warehouse and shopping centre operator BTC led the day's decliners, falling 3.49 percent to 14,120 tolars on volume of 294 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
